tagline.text: Sagada's highest peak, a half-day hike through pine forest and open grassland ridges

location.label: Location
location.text: Ambasing, Sagada, Mountain Province (trailhead at Ambasing Elementary School)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱0~1,500 (depending on guide and jeepney use, for a group of 1–10)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL), about 12 hours overland

children.text: Mount Ampacao rises above the village of Ambasing, southwest of Sagada town, at about 1,889 m, the highest point in Sagada. Climbing through pine forest and a ranch-like grassland ridge to the summit takes around 2 hours, and many people hike it at dawn or as a traverse to Lake Danum.

Mount Ampacao is the highest peak in Sagada, Mountain Province, in the Cordillera region of northern Philippines, and several hiking accounts give its elevation as about 1,889 m. Sagada town itself sits at about 1,500 m above sea level, so the climb from town to the summit is roughly 400 m. The Philippine mountaineering site Pinoy Mountaineer classes it as a minor climb, difficulty 2/9, and describes it as a half-day trip. It feels like a hill a little taller than a typical neighborhood hill back home, so it is not physically demanding.

The trailhead is Ambasing Elementary School in Ambasing village, within walking distance of Sagada town. The hike starts on a steep concrete road, soon turns into a dirt and rocky trail shaded by pines, and about two-thirds of the way up opens onto a grassland ridge known as "the ranch." The view here is the best on the mountain, so many people mistake it for the summit. The real summit is where a cell-site tower stands, about 20–30 minutes further up from the ranch.

There are three reasons this mountain is popular with Sagada visitors. First, the route is simple, and many people walk it without a guide. Second, from the ridge you can see both the Sagada side and the western Besao side, and on clear days the view extends to mountain ranges toward Ilocos. Third, you can continue over the summit and down through the pines to Lake Danum, so you can combine a mountain and a lake in half a day. It is also less crowded than the famous Kiltepan sunrise viewpoint, which makes it an alternative for anyone who wants a quieter dawn.

Note that this guide is not based on on-site signage but on comparing many hikers' accounts and travel information. Many of the accounts used date from 2012 to 2016, so fees and rules may differ today. Be sure to check the latest information at the Sagada tourism office.

The summit, at about 1,889 m, has a cell-site tower. To the west you can see the mountain ridges along the Ilocos Sur and Abra boundary, and in good visibility you can also make out Mount Polis to the southeast, the Tirad Pass area to the east, and Mount Sipsipitan to the north.

This open ridge about two-thirds of the way up the mountain gives 360-degree views. It is windy and chilly, and you cool down quickly once you stop sweating. It is the best spot for photos, so most people rest here.

Once the concrete road ends, the trail becomes a dirt path under continuous pine shade. The shade makes walking easier even in the heat of the day, and hikers report enjoying woodpecker marks, unfamiliar plants and wildflowers along the way.

Along the way up you can look down on Sagada's Kapay-aw rice terraces. The color of the fields changes between the June–July planting season and before harvest, so you see a different scene depending on the time of year.

blocks.title: Dawn hike and sea of clouds

children.text: Many hikers start before dawn to catch the sunrise. On foggy days, however, visibility around the summit has been reported at only a few meters, so you may end up enjoying the view on the way down as the clouds lift.
There is a traverse from the summit down the far side through forest and a few ups and downs to Lake Danum. One account estimated about
3 hours
from the summit to the lake, and the lake is about
4 km
from Sagada town. Watching the sunset beside the lake is also popular.

Cattle graze around the ranch, and wooden gates keep them from leaving. Please close the gate behind you after passing. Even on weekends it is quieter than other Sagada attractions, so you can enjoy a relaxed hike.

items.title: Dawn sunrise hike (round trip)
items.subtitle: Start in the dark and return to town in the morning

children.text: Set out from your lodging with a headlamp and walk toward Ambasing Elementary School. At the fork, take the uphill road on the right.
Pass through the pine forest and reach the ranch grassland. Close the wooden gate behind you after passing. Enjoy the view as daylight arrives.
From the gate, take the side trail on the left and follow the power lines up to the summit cell site. Have a snack and rest at the summit.
Come back down the same way, take one more look at the view from the ranch, and descend.
Return to Sagada town for breakfast, then continue with a cave or waterfall activity in the afternoon.
The times are rough estimates combined from several accounts. They vary depending on whether the walk from town to the trailhead (about
40 minutes
) is included, so allow plenty of time.

items.title: Lake Danum traverse
items.subtitle: Over the summit and on to the lake for sunset, about 6 hours

children.text: Take a jeepney or van to Ambasing village, or walk to the trailhead.
Pass the ranch and summit and start the downhill through the pine forest. Rest at the summit for about
15 minutes
After a steep descent and one short climb, arrive at Lake Danum.
Watch the sunset at the lake, then walk the roughly
4 km
to town or take a car you arranged in advance.

On days when daylight is short, the descent toward the lake can get dark quickly, so it is safest to start by around noon at the latest. The route has places where trails split, so on a first visit we recommend going with a guide from the Sagada tourism office.
A night bus from Manila, either direct or via Baguio and Bontoc, reaches Sagada the following morning. One hiker's account lists an evening
departure from Manila with a fare of around
. The distance is long, so it is an overnight trip of about
12 hours
Another way is to take a bus from Manila to Baguio and transfer there to a Lizardo bus to Sagada.
Bus companies, departure times and fares change often. Check the latest schedules at the Manila bus terminal and at the Sagada bus stop.

children.text: From Sagada town to Ambasing Elementary School it is about
40 minutes
on foot, uphill enough to work up a light sweat.
To save time you can hire a jeepney or van to Ambasing village. Past accounts list about
one way to the trailhead and about

items.title: Returning from the mountain to town

children.text: If you come back down the way you went up, it is about
40 minutes
on foot from the trailhead to town.
If you traverse to Lake Danum, it is about
4 km
from the lake to Sagada town, and some people arrange a car to wait on the paved road near the lake.

The dry season, November to May, is best. Clear mornings give the cleanest views. Because Sagada is high, it is cool even at midday, and the dawn and the summit ridge are bitterly windy. Hail showers are said to occur on some winter days.

In the June–October rainy season the trail is slippery and fog limits visibility. Still, hikers report that walking through the pine forest is pleasant even in drizzle, so bring rain gear and waterproof shoes and go with a guide.

rows: Clear and cool, very cold at dawn
Best views, and a thick jacket is needed for a dawn hike.
Dry and clear, hot at midday
Walk early in the morning and avoid the midday sun.
Short visibility and a muddy trail, so decide carefully.

items.note: One account says no entrance fee or permit is needed for the mountain itself, but check the Sagada tourism office registration and environmental fee separately.

Lodging is concentrated in Sagada town. If you are going for a dawn hike, guesthouses in the town center are closest to the trailhead, and it is common to stay a night or two and combine the hike with caves and waterfalls. Options range from dorms to private rooms, and during the peak season of December to May, weekend rooms fill quickly.

Meals are had at restaurants in town. Eat a solid breakfast before the hike and bring plenty of snacks and water for the trail. One account says the hiker rested after descending at a well-known cafe in town with mountain tea and lemon pie.
If you leave town before dawn, a headlamp is essential. It is easy to take a wrong turn in the dark early section.
At the fork near the trailhead, take the uphill road on the right (the concrete road). A local advised that the left road is rough.
The summit is still far from the ranch. Take the left side trail with the wooden gate and follow the power lines another 20–30 minutes to reach the cell-site tower.
The wooden gates around the ranch keep cattle from leaving, so please close them behind you.
There are slippery slopes, so trekking poles help, and for the traverse where the route is confusing, going with a guide gives peace of mind.
If you hire a guide, confirm in advance whether they will take you to the summit and whether Lake Danum is included.
Bring a light windbreaker and a thick jacket for the summit wind and the dawn cold.
Safety and environmental rules in the Sagada area change from year to year. Check the latest notices at the tourism office before you set out.
In the dark before dawn you may meet aggressive dogs or lose visibility in fog, so go with a companion or a guide rather than alone.
In dense fog, visibility on the grassland ridge drops to a few meters and it is easy to miss a fork.
After rain the clay-like dirt trail is slippery, and hikers report leeches, so long sleeves and long pants are safer.
There is a record that lightning has struck the summit cell-site tower. If thunder and lightning start, do not stay on the ridge and descend immediately.
You cannot tell whether water along the trail is safe to drink, so it is better to carry your own drinking water.
On the road near town you may meet unleashed dogs. Do not run suddenly, and pass slowly.
The town below the mountain. Hanging coffins, Echo Valley, cafes and the tourism office are clustered here, making it a good stop before or after the hike. It is about
40 minutes
on foot from town to the trailhead.
A lake in a pine forest, reached by descending the far side from the summit, about
4 km
from town. It is known as a sunset walk.
Sagada's signature cave route, which many people do after the hike. The connection route requires a guide, and one account says it takes around
3 hours
A small waterfall visited after the cave outing. Hiker accounts describe combining the mountain, caves and the falls in one day.
Sagada's most famous sunrise spot. If you want to avoid the crowds and enjoy a quiet dawn, Ampacao is an alternative.
